title: Architecture analysis: improve the generalized BRC reviewer (A + B small)
problem_statement: The pipeline's BRC reviewer_code is confirming consensus while missing genuine blocking issues that the GHA egg-reviewer then flags after the PR is opened (PR #1964 is the canonical example: an uncommitted sandbox/scripts/jira deliverable, and a /api/v1/jira/execute path=project allowlist bypass). The desired outcome is that any blocking issue is caught and fixed inside the pipeline. The issue body has pre-resolved scope to A + B (small): subagent delegation inside reviewer_code for large diffs, plus two new specialised reviewer roles (reviewer_security, reviewer_concurrency). Both ship as ADVISORY on day 1, no severity rubric or attestation models, and only REVIEWER-SYNC.md is touched on the GHA side.
in_scope: A — Subagent delegation block inside reviewer_code prompt (threshold-gated; reviewer self-gates and self-fans-out using the Claude Agent SDK Task tool).
B — Two new ADVISORY reviewer roles: reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency, with dedicated criteria files that inherit from code-review-criteria.md.
REVIEWER-SYNC.md update documenting the SDLC-only asymmetry (new criteria files + subagent fan-out are SDLC-only).
Per-pipeline parallelism knob: phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel field on the contract (default true).
Regression-replay test for PR #1964 with two modes (CI-unconditional prompt asserts + opt-in live-LLM gated by RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1).

Verification (not redefinition) that the existing role_value.replace('reviewer_', '', 1).replace('_', '-') mapping at pipelines.py:8317 already routes reviewer_security → security and reviewer_concurrency → concurrency.
out_of_scope: Severity-tagged NACK flagging (#1997 — pairs with B; new reviewers stay ADVISORY until then).
GHA reviewer code (action/build-review-prompt.sh, action/reusable-review.yml). Only REVIEWER-SYNC.md is updated.
Adding a redundant reviewer_type mapping dict/elif chain — the existing one-liner already handles both new roles.
Adding REVIEWER_ATTESTATION_MODELS entries for the two new reviewers (Pitfall 4 — only add if day-1 ACKs carry attestation payloads, which they do not).

current_architecture_summary.agent_roles_canonical: shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py — AgentRole StrEnum is the canonical source of truth. Existing reviewer roles (REVIEWER_CODE, REVIEWER_CONTRACT, REVIEWER_AGENT_DESIGN, REVIEWER_REFINE, REVIEWER_PLAN) follow the same pattern: enum entry + AgentRoleDefinition with allowed/blocked file_access + AGENT_ROLES registry + AGENT_ROLE_TO_CONTRACT_ROLE mapping (Role.REVIEWER) + _PHASE_REVIEWERS list + (optional) EGG_ONLY_REVIEWERS membership.
current_architecture_summary.review_graph: orchestrator/review_graph.py — get_default_implement_graph() builds the asymmetric edge list. ReviewCriticality has CRITICAL and ADVISORY. Adding ReviewEdge(reviewer_security, coder, ADVISORY), ReviewEdge(reviewer_security, tester, ADVISORY), ReviewEdge(reviewer_concurrency, coder, ADVISORY), ReviewEdge(reviewer_concurrency, tester, ADVISORY) is mechanical.
current_architecture_summary.criteria_loader_dispatch: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py — _get_review_criteria_for_type() at L3244 is a string-key dispatch (agent-design / code / contract / refine / plan). Adding security/concurrency branches is mechanical, mirroring the code-review loader (which uses _read_shared_criteria with a user_override fallback path and an inline-fallback string).
current_architecture_summary.scope_preamble: _get_reviewer_scope_preamble() at L3262 — same string-key dispatch; needs new branches for security/concurrency telling the reviewer to ONLY flag issues in its lens (delegating non-lens findings to reviewer_code).
current_architecture_summary.review_prompt_builder: _build_review_prompt() at L4217 has reviewer_type='code' branch with procedural steps, conventions, NACK-vs-ACK section. Currently does NOT have the diff text or the contract; pitfall-2 / pitfall-3 decisions both keep the function lean by self-gating in the prompt rather than threading new arguments.
current_architecture_summary.reviewer_role_to_type_mapping: pipelines.py:8317 already does role_value.replace('reviewer_', '', 1).replace('_', '-'). reviewer_security → 'security', reviewer_concurrency → 'concurrency' fall out automatically; this must be verified (unit test) but NOT replaced with a dict.
current_architecture_summary.phase_config_schema: shared/egg_contracts/models.py PhaseConfig currently has only checks/max_review_cycles/human_review_mechanism. To support phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel, the schema needs a new optional nested field (e.g. reviewer_code: Optional[ReviewerCodeConfig]={parallel: bool=True}), with phase_defaults.py merge logic preserving the override.
current_architecture_summary.shared_criteria_files: shared/prompts/ contains code-review-criteria.md (canonical, read by both GHA and SDLC), contract-review-criteria.md, agent-design-criteria.md, REVIEWER-SYNC.md. Add security-review-criteria.md and concurrency-review-criteria.md alongside.
current_architecture_summary.agent_sdk_subagent_tool: shared/egg_agent/client.py L162-167 only blocks WebFetch / WebSearch in private mode. The Claude Agent SDK Task subagent tool is NOT blocked anywhere — no allow-list edits, no MCP plumbing, no tool-registry additions, no orchestrator routing changes are needed for reviewer_code to spawn subagents. This is purely a prompt change (decision-10).
current_architecture_summary.attestation_schemas: orchestrator/attestation_schemas.py REVIEWER_ATTESTATION_MODELS only registers reviewer_code, reviewer_contract, tester. validate_attestation in peer_consensus.py is gated on review.attestation truthy, so reviewers without models work fine (reviewer_refine, reviewer_agent_design, reviewer_plan ship without models today). Day-1 ACKs from reviewer_security / reviewer_concurrency will not carry attestation payloads → do NOT add models (Pitfall 4).
current_architecture_summary.integration_test_layout: integration_tests/sdlc/ has conftest.py, test_happy_path.py, test_hitl_flow.py, test_refine_plan_review_cycles.py, test_review_rejection.py, test_role_enforcement.py. There is no fixtures/ directory yet — adding integration_tests/sdlc/fixtures/1964-diff.patch and integration_tests/sdlc/test_reviewer_1964_regression.py is greenfield.

recommended_architecture.summary: Implement A + B small as a prompt-and-config change with surgical Python additions. No new MCP verbs, no new orchestrator routes, no new sandbox tools. The reviewer_code prompt grows a self-gated subagent fan-out block (Option 2B/3B + decision-3 OR composition + decision-4 path-glob slicing), the agent_roles enum gains two new StrEnum members (auto-routing through the existing one-liner reviewer_type mapping at pipelines.py:8317), the review_graph implement-phase factory gains four ADVISORY edges, _get_review_criteria_for_type() and _get_reviewer_scope_preamble() each gain two branches (security, concurrency) backed by two new shared/prompts criteria files that explicitly Inherit from code-review-criteria.md, and PhaseConfig gains a small reviewer_code config block (parallel: bool = true) consumed by the prompt builder when emitting the fan-out instruction. A regression-replay test pinned to PR #1964's diff (1964-diff.patch) asserts both previously-missed issues are flagged in two modes: CI-unconditional prompt-text asserts plus an opt-in live-LLM replay gated by RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1.

components.name: New reviewer roles in agent_roles.py
responsibilities: Add AgentRole.REVIEWER_SECURITY = 'reviewer_security' and AgentRole.REVIEWER_CONCURRENCY = 'reviewer_concurrency' StrEnum members.

Add REVIEWER_SECURITY_ROLE and REVIEWER_CONCURRENCY_ROLE AgentRoleDefinition instances modelled after REVIEWER_PLAN_ROLE/REVIEWER_CODE_ROLE: REVIEW category, depends on TASK_PLANNER+RISK_ANALYST (same as reviewer_code), file_access allows .egg-state/reviews/ + .egg-state/agent-outputs/ with _REVIEWER_BLOCKED_WRITE.
Wire both into AGENT_ROLES dict and AGENT_ROLE_TO_CONTRACT_ROLE (both → Role.REVIEWER).
Append both to _PHASE_REVIEWERS['implement'] so get_roles_for_phase('implement') includes them by default. They are NOT egg-only (omit from EGG_ONLY_REVIEWERS).
Update the REVIEW role docstring on AgentRole to include the two new entries.
components.rationale: Mirrors the additive pattern used for REVIEWER_REFINE / REVIEWER_AGENT_DESIGN. No schema migration; all dependent helpers (validate_roles_for_custom_phase, get_roles_for_phase, get_role_definition) work by virtue of registration.

components.name: Review graph edges for the implement phase
responsibilities: Inside get_default_implement_graph() add four new edges: ReviewEdge('reviewer_security', 'coder', ADVISORY), ReviewEdge('reviewer_security', 'tester', ADVISORY), ReviewEdge('reviewer_concurrency', 'coder', ADVISORY), ReviewEdge('reviewer_concurrency', 'tester', ADVISORY).
Update the docstring listing producers/reviewers.
components.rationale: ADVISORY criticality makes the new reviewers non-deadlocking — their NACKs surface as warnings but cannot block consensus, satisfying decision-11 and matching the day-1 promotion-deferred-to-#1997 plan.

components.name: Two dedicated criteria files in shared/prompts/
responsibilities: Both files open with an explicit header: 'Inherits from code-review-criteria.md; only the lens-specific rules below override or extend it.' (decision-5).

security-review-criteria.md focuses the reviewer on OWASP top-10 cross-file flow problems, secret leakage, allowlist/denylist mismatches between handler and validator (the PR #1964 ^project$ failure mode), authentication/authorization paths, SSRF/SSRF-equivalents, deserialization, supply-chain (uncommitted dependencies / dangling symlinks like the PR #1964 sandbox/scripts/jira failure mode).

concurrency-review-criteria.md focuses the reviewer on race conditions, deadlocks, missing locks, atomicity boundaries, async event-loop pitfalls, BRC consensus protocol invariants (re-review, ACK/NACK ordering, timing), and resource lifecycle (file handles, subprocess wait, asyncio task cancellation).
Both files explicitly DEFER non-lens findings to reviewer_code — the lens reviewers only flag inside their lens; comprehensive coverage is reviewer_code's responsibility (still ADVISORY-coexists).
components.rationale: Lens-focused inheritance keeps the new criteria small, prevents accidental criteria duplication, and respects the REVIEWER-SYNC inline-fallback parity by giving each loader a clear inline fallback string.

components.name: Criteria loaders + scope preambles in pipelines.py
responsibilities: Add _get_security_review_criteria(repo_path) and _get_concurrency_review_criteria(repo_path) using the same shape as _get_code_review_criteria (read shared file via _read_shared_criteria, fall back to an inline string that mirrors the dedicated md file's substance).
Extend _get_review_criteria_for_type() to dispatch reviewer_type='security' and reviewer_type='concurrency'.

Extend _get_reviewer_scope_preamble() with branches for 'security' and 'concurrency' that explicitly say 'this is a specialised lens review — do NOT review code quality or correctness in general; defer those to reviewer_code'.
components.rationale: Reuses the existing pattern. The 'reviewer_security' role string flows through the existing role_value.replace('reviewer_','').replace('_','-') one-liner at pipelines.py:8317 and lands as reviewer_type='security' — no new mapping needed (Pitfall 1 verified).

components.name: Subagent fan-out block inside reviewer_code prompt (with parent cross-partition pass)
responsibilities: Inside _build_review_prompt() under the existing if reviewer_type == 'code' branch, append a self-gated subagent fan-out instruction block that tells the reviewer to: (1) run git diff --numstat <base>...HEAD; (2) compute (files_changed, loc); (3) IF files_changed > 10 OR loc > 500 (decision-3 OR composition), call mcp__sdlc__show_contract and self-extract phases.implement.tasks[]; (4) partition the changed files by logical subsystem inferred from the task list — with a soft cap of ≤6 subagents (when implement-phase tasks exceed 6, group adjacent / related tasks into combined partitions until the count falls to ≤6); (5) dispatch one Task subagent per partition (parallel by default per the contract's reviewer_code.parallel knob); (6) each Task subagent re-runs git diff <base>...HEAD -- <path-globs-for-its-partition> itself and reviews the slice against code-review-criteria.md, reporting findings as a structured list; each subagent caps its own wall-clock budget at ~5 minutes and emits an mcp__brc__send_heartbeat or mcp__progress__emit at start/end so the parent can detect stalls.

**(7) MANDATORY PARENT CROSS-PARTITION PASS** — after subagents return, the parent reviewer (still in the reviewer_code session) MUST run `git diff <base>...HEAD` itself (full unfiltered diff) and perform a cross-file invariants pass focused on the failure modes that PR #1964 actually exhibited: (a) handler ↔ allowlist consistency (does each route handler validate against the project/path allowlist its extractor advertises?); (b) route ↔ schema consistency (do request/response shapes match across files?); (c) fixture ↔ Dockerfile/runtime reference consistency (does every script/symlink/binary referenced by Dockerfile, compose files, or systemd units exist as a committed file in the diff or repo?); (d) any other cross-file invariants the lens reviewers (reviewer_security, reviewer_concurrency) flagged via their ADVISORY edges. The parent emits findings from this pass alongside the aggregated subagent findings in the final ACK/NACK reason. This step is REQUIRED by issue #1965's primary acceptance criterion ("anything blocking should be caught and fixed inside the pipeline"); without it, partition-spanning cross-file bugs (the exact PR #1964 ^project$ failure mode) slip through because day-1 reviewer_security/reviewer_concurrency are ADVISORY and cannot block consensus.
(8) Parent aggregates subagent findings + cross-partition-pass findings into a single ACK/NACK reason.

Provide an explicit fallback path: if implement-phase tasks are empty (e.g. custom-phase invocation), skip fan-out and review yourself end-to-end (decision-3B fallback). The mandatory parent cross-partition pass still runs (since you are the parent reviewing the full diff anyway).

MCP unavailability contingency for decision-2 (3B): if mcp__sdlc__show_contract is unreachable from the parent's session at fan-out time, the parent emits an mcp__progress__emit warning and falls back to skipping fan-out (review yourself end-to-end with the cross-partition pass). If MCP is reachable from the parent but unreachable from a Task subagent (e.g. the SDK does not propagate MCP server access into subagents — a load-bearing decision-10 assumption flagged in R-9 below), the parent fetches the partition spec via mcp__sdlc__show_contract once and inlines the partition list in each subagent prompt. Implementation should land a thin probe + fallback (one boolean check at fan-out time) so the implementation does not have to redesign mid-coding.

Provide a 'log the gate decision' instruction telling the reviewer to use mcp__brc__send_heartbeat (state=WORKING) or mcp__progress__emit (step='reviewer_code.fan_out', state='working', detail='...') recording 'Subagent fan-out: enabled (N partitions, M files, L LOC)' or '...skipped (below threshold)' or '...skipped (empty implement-phase tasks)'. Prefer the structured progress/heartbeat surfaces over `egg-orch message send --type STATUS` because they are easier to grep historically and are persisted on the orchestrator's progress bus.

Pull the parallelism knob via a new optional argument on _build_review_prompt() and on _build_phase_prompt() (reviewer_code_parallel: bool = True), defaulted from get_effective_phase_config(contract, IMPLEMENT).reviewer_code.parallel. Thread it from the call site at L8318 where the contract is in scope (or fall back to True if the contract is None / phase_configs absent).
components.rationale: Pure prompt change for the reviewer's behaviour (decision-2B + decision-3B + decision-4). The mandatory parent cross-partition pass (step 7) closes the cross-file blind spot that motivated issue #1965 in the first place — without it, the architecture would reproduce the PR #1964 failure mode by construction. The parallelism flag is the ONLY orchestrator-side wiring needed and lives entirely on the contract via existing PhaseConfig override semantics. No diff plumbing in Python (Option 2A rejected); no contract loader in Python (Option 3A rejected); no patch-fragment slicing in the parent (decision-4 keeps the parent's job small for fan-out itself, while step 7 deliberately re-fetches the full diff in the parent for cross-cutting invariants). Soft cap of ≤6 subagents and 5-minute per-subagent budget bound the fan-out blast radius (mitigates risk-2/risk-7/risk-16). MCP-unavailability contingency makes decision-10's load-bearing assumption falsifiable at fan-out time rather than mid-implementation.

components.name: PhaseConfig.reviewer_code knob
responsibilities: Add a new ReviewerCodeConfig BaseModel with parallel: bool = Field(default=True). Add reviewer_code: Optional[ReviewerCodeConfig] = None to PhaseConfig.
Update get_effective_phase_config() to merge contract.phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code over the default (None → defaults; partial → take override).
Default in _DEFAULT_PHASE_CONFIGS[IMPLEMENT] explicitly sets reviewer_code=ReviewerCodeConfig(parallel=True) so contracts that don't set it still get parallel by default (feedback-11).
components.rationale: Keeps the parallelism switch on the contract per decision-6. PhaseConfig is already the schema for per-phase overrides, so no new top-level surface is required and CLI tooling that reads contracts inherits the field for free.

components.name: Reviewer-sync doc update
responsibilities: Add a section documenting the SDLC-only asymmetry: reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency are SDLC-only ADVISORY reviewers (no GHA equivalent); GHA reviewer code (action/...) is intentionally untouched.

Add the subagent fan-out behaviour to the 'What's Intentionally Different' table — SDLC reviewer_code conditionally fans out via Task subagents when diff > 10 files OR > 500 LOC; GHA reviewer does not.
Update the Modification Checklist: when changing reviewer_security / reviewer_concurrency criteria, update both the shared/prompts file and the inline fallback string in pipelines.py.
components.rationale: Feedback-9 and the issue's GHA-untouched constraint require an explicit doc record so future maintainers don't accidentally try to mirror these into action/.

components.name: Regression-replay test for PR #1964
responsibilities: Store the fixture as a Python module exporting a string constant (PR_1964_DIFF: str = '''...''') in integration_tests/sdlc/fixtures/pr_1964_diff.py — NOT as a `.patch` file. Rationale: TESTER_ROLE.file_access in shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py:243-298 only allows-write **/*.py / yaml / json / toml / source extensions; a push that adds a `.patch` file from the tester role is rejected by the gateway. The Python-string approach round-trips through the same gateway constraints used everywhere else in the test suite.

Test mode 1 — CI-unconditional prompt asserts: build the reviewer_code prompt for a synthetic state where get_diff_metrics returns (12 files, 800 LOC); assert the rendered prompt contains the subagent-fan-out block AND the parent cross-partition-pass markers (per the C5 step-7 amendment). Repeat for (3 files, 50 LOC) and assert the fan-out block is NOT present, but the cross-partition-pass section is still present (the parent always reads the full diff for cross-cutting invariants — this is decoupled from threshold gating).

Test mode 2 — opt-in live-LLM: gated by RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1 environment variable; uses the real Anthropic SDK client to drive a reviewer_code session against PR_1964_DIFF; asserts the reviewer's ACK/NACK reason text contains references to BOTH the uncommitted sandbox/scripts/jira issue AND the ^project$ allowlist-bypass issue. The latter directly exercises the C5 step-7 cross-partition pass.
Add a fixture loader and a small helper for the reviewer_code prompt builder that feeds a stubbed contract with implement-phase tasks (so the partition path runs).
components.rationale: Decision-7 selected 'both modes'. CI-unconditional prompt asserts give regression-protection without LLM cost (catches accidental removal of the fan-out block); the opt-in live-LLM mode is the genuine end-to-end exercise but stays out of the default CI cost path.

components.name: Verification-only unit tests for existing wiring
responsibilities: Add a unit test asserting the existing one-liner at pipelines.py:8317 maps reviewer_security → 'security' and reviewer_concurrency → 'concurrency' (Pitfall 1).
Add a unit test asserting that a reviewer_security ACK with empty attestation passes validate_attestation (Pitfall 4 — confirms the no-model path works).

Add a complementary NEGATIVE unit test asserting that a reviewer_security ACK with NON-empty attestation raises a clear ValueError naming the unregistered role, so an accidental day-1 attestation payload from a future agent fails fast instead of silently round-tripping (covers risk_analyst risk-5 / accidental-payload deadlock).
Add unit tests for new criteria loaders, the new scope preamble branches, and the new PhaseConfig.reviewer_code merge semantics.
components.rationale: Verification rather than invention; ensures the no-redundant-mapping and no-attestation-models invariants stay protected against future drift.

components.name: Documentation refresh
responsibilities: Add a brief subsection to docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md describing reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency as ADVISORY day-1 reviewers and pointing readers at the criteria files.
Add a paragraph to docs/architecture/orchestrator.md noting that reviewer_code conditionally fans out via Task subagents above ~10 files / ~500 LOC, with the threshold defined in-prompt (Option 2B).
components.rationale: Two short doc deltas keep architecture/concurrency-execution docs in sync with the new behaviour. Keeps these scoped to ADVISORY-status promotion notes (no severity rubric content here).

key_technical_decisions.decision: reviewer_code self-gates the threshold check by running git diff --numstat in-prompt (Option 2B).
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Avoids orchestrator-side numstat plumbing; matches the existing pattern of telling the reviewer to run git diff itself; non-determinism mitigated by the regression-replay prompt-text asserts (which check that the reviewer prompt instructs the gate, not whether the reviewer's runtime gate decision is correct).
key_technical_decisions.implication: _build_review_prompt() does NOT gain (files_changed, loc) parameters. The reviewer's prompt embeds the threshold rule as plain text.

key_technical_decisions.decision: reviewer_code fetches the implement-phase task list via mcp__sdlc__show_contract from its own session (Option 3B), with explicit fallback: empty implement-phase tasks → skip fan-out.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Keeps _build_review_prompt() lean; agents already use MCP for contract reads; aligns with the broader pattern.
key_technical_decisions.implication: No contract parameter on _build_review_prompt(). The reviewer is instructed to call mcp__sdlc__show_contract and self-extract phases.implement.tasks[].

key_technical_decisions.decision: Threshold composition is OR — fan-out triggers when files_changed > 10 OR loc > 500.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Either trip is a strong-enough signal that the diff is too large for a single review pass; AND would let high-LOC single-file refactors slip through.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Prompt text says 'if files > 10 OR loc > 500' verbatim.

key_technical_decisions.decision: Each subagent re-runs git diff itself and filters by path glob to its assigned partition; the parent reviewer passes only the partition spec.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the parent's responsibilities minimal (no diff slicing, no patch-fragment handling); subagents already have shell access; matches the 'agents fetch their own context' pattern.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Prompt text instructs subagents to run git diff <base>...HEAD -- <glob1> <glob2> ... limited to their assigned paths.

key_technical_decisions.decision: security-review-criteria.md and concurrency-review-criteria.md inherit from code-review-criteria.md via an explicit header.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Prevents accidental criteria duplication; keeps REVIEWER-SYNC.md honest; reviewers know they apply lens-specific overrides on top of the canonical criteria.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Each new file opens with: 'Inherits from code-review-criteria.md; only lens-specific rules below override or extend it.' Loaders for security/concurrency call _read_shared_criteria for their dedicated file (no auto-merging — the inherit is by reference, the reviewer reads both).

key_technical_decisions.decision: Per-pipeline subagent parallelism knob lives in phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel (default true).
key_technical_decisions.rationale: PhaseConfig already exists for per-phase overrides; using it gives free CLI/API plumbing and avoids env vars / settings.json entanglement.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Add ReviewerCodeConfig BaseModel; add reviewer_code field to PhaseConfig; update phase_defaults merge logic; thread the bool from the call site at L8318 into _build_review_prompt(reviewer_code_parallel=...).

key_technical_decisions.decision: PR #1964 regression-replay ships in BOTH modes — CI-unconditional prompt-text asserts AND opt-in live-LLM gated by RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: Prompt-text asserts catch accidental removal of the fan-out block in normal CI; live-LLM mode validates the actual model behaviour but stays out of the default CI cost budget.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Two test functions in test_reviewer_1964_regression.py — the first deterministic and unconditional, the second gated by os.environ.get('RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY') == '1' (skip otherwise).

key_technical_decisions.decision: Use the Claude Agent SDK's built-in Task subagent tool (decision-10 from the issue body).
key_technical_decisions.rationale: shared/egg_agent/client.py:162-167 only blocks WebFetch/WebSearch in private mode; Task is unblocked, so no allow-list edits, no MCP verb, no orchestrator routing.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Subagent fan-out is purely a prompt instruction. Subagents inherit the parent's tool roster automatically via the SDK.

key_technical_decisions.decision: Both new reviewers ship as ADVISORY on day 1 (no day-1 attestation models).
key_technical_decisions.rationale: ADVISORY edges cannot deadlock consensus; promotion to CRITICAL waits for #1997 (severity-tagged NACK flagging). validate_attestation in peer_consensus.py is conditional on review.attestation truthy — reviewers without attestation models work fine, as proven by reviewer_refine, reviewer_agent_design, reviewer_plan.
key_technical_decisions.implication: Do NOT add ReviewerSecurityAttestation / ReviewerConcurrencyAttestation classes. Do NOT register entries in REVIEWER_ATTESTATION_MODELS.

key_technical_decisions.decision: Do NOT introduce a redundant reviewer_type mapping dict / if-elif chain.
key_technical_decisions.rationale: pipelines.py:8317 already does role_value.replace('reviewer_', '', 1).replace('_', '-'); adding a dict would be net-negative.
key_technical_decisions.implication: C9 ships a unit-test that asserts this mapping behaves correctly for the two new roles; no production-code addition.

constraints: GHA reviewer code is OFF-LIMITS — only shared/prompts/REVIEWER-SYNC.md is updated on the GHA side.
Backward compatibility: existing reviewer roles, edges, and prompts must keep working unchanged.
Day-1 cost / latency budget: 2-5x cost on large PRs, 5-10 min latency, no hard per-pipeline ceiling.
Threshold gate: below 10 changed files OR 500 LOC, fan-out is off by default. Above either, on by default. Reviewer can override either direction at its discretion.
Acceptance is trend-based — GHA blocking-count per pipeline-PR trends to zero across N PRs. No hard numeric gate.
Phase boundary: refine/plan reviewers do NOT get subagent fan-out; only reviewer_code does.
ADVISORY criticality on day 1 for both new reviewers — promotion to CRITICAL is gated on #1997.
Architect file restrictions: this output writes only to .egg-state/agent-outputs/1965-architect-output.json; no production code, no contracts, no drafts.

internal: shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py (canonical AgentRole enum) — must export the two new members or downstream gateway/agent_restrictions.py role-string validation will reject them.
orchestrator/review_graph.py — implement-phase factory must include the four new ADVISORY edges or BRC will not invoke the new reviewers.
shared/egg_contracts/models.py + phase_defaults.py — PhaseConfig change must round-trip through gateway contract endpoints (Pydantic v2 backward-compat).
shared/prompts/code-review-criteria.md — referenced by inheritance header in the two new criteria files; no edits required.
external: None — Task subagent tool is built into the Claude Agent SDK (no version bump required); current shared/egg_agent/client.py already permits it.
Anthropic API — only used by the opt-in live-LLM regression-replay path; default CI doesn't invoke it.
cross_repo: GHA reviewer code (action/) is intentionally untouched.
REVIEWER-SYNC.md is the only sync artifact; modification checklist updates ensure future drift is caught.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Self-gated threshold (TD-1) is non-deterministic — the reviewer might decide differently on different runs even with the same diff.
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: Regression-replay prompt asserts (TD-7 mode 1) verify the prompt instructs the gate; live-LLM mode (TD-7 mode 2) verifies the gate is honoured end-to-end on a known fixture.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Subagent fan-out cost (2-5× on large PRs per feedback-1) could escalate if subagents themselves trigger nested Task calls or run for unbounded turns.
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: C5 caps subagent count at ≤6 (implement-phase tasks > 6 are grouped). Each subagent has a ~5-minute wall-clock budget enforced by prompt-side guidance. Subagents are explicitly instructed not to nest Task calls. Total cost stays inside feedback-1's 2-5× envelope on large PRs.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: ADVISORY edges produce noisy NACKs that humans/operators ignore until #1997 lands.
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: Day-1 advisory status by design (decision-11). Document promotion path in REVIEWER-SYNC.md and docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: PhaseConfig schema change (C6) could break existing serialised contracts on disk if the new field is required.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Subagent fan-out partition strategy (Option 3B/decision-4) may produce uneven load if implement-phase tasks are skewed (e.g., 80% of LOC in one task).
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: Reviewer can override partition heuristic at its discretion (the prompt allows free-form partitioning); the empty-tasks fallback skips fan-out entirely.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Subagent diff-glob filtering (decision-4) may miss cross-file findings that span partition boundaries (e.g., a route handler in partition A whose allowlist extractor lives in partition B — the exact PR #1964 ^project$ failure mode).
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: C5 step-7 makes the parent cross-partition pass MANDATORY (no longer escalated to a follow-up issue) — the parent reviewer reads the full unfiltered diff and explicitly checks handler ↔ allowlist consistency, route ↔ schema consistency, and fixture ↔ Dockerfile reference consistency before issuing ACK/NACK. The regression-replay test (mode 2) asserts both PR #1964 cross-partition issues are flagged. reviewer_security's lens-specific criteria additionally call this out, providing a second (ADVISORY) layer of detection.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Decision-10 (Task subagent tool from the Claude Agent SDK) is a load-bearing assumption that has not been stress-tested in this repo. If MCP server access does not propagate into Task subagents, decision-2 (3B reviewer self-fetch via mcp__sdlc__show_contract) collapses for subagents.
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: C5 specifies a probe + fallback: parent fetches the partition spec via mcp__sdlc__show_contract once and inlines it in subagent prompts when MCP is unreachable from a subagent. If MCP is also unreachable from the parent, fan-out is skipped entirely (the parent reviews end-to-end with the cross-partition pass). The implementation lands the probe as a single boolean check at fan-out time, so the fallback kicks in deterministically rather than mid-coding. risk_analyst should treat decision-10 viability as a smoke-spike candidate during the implement phase's first task; if the spike fails, fall back to Option 3A (orchestrator-side contract loader) is documented.

risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.description: Without an upper bound, fan-out could spawn dozens of subagents on contracts with many implement-phase tasks (e.g., 30+ tasks); BRC heartbeat starvation under blocking subagents could delay the consensus loop and trip overseer alerts.
risks_handed_to_risk_analyst.mitigation: C5 sets a soft cap of ≤6 subagents (related tasks are grouped above the cap). Each subagent emits an mcp__brc__send_heartbeat at start/end so the parent and orchestrator can detect stalls. Per-subagent 5-minute wall-clock budget bounds the worst-case latency.

complexity_assessment.rating: medium (with one load-bearing assumption to validate early)
complexity_assessment.rationale: Touches ~10 files (2 enum entries, 4 review-graph edges, 2 new criteria docs + 2 inline fallbacks, 2 prompt builder branches, 1 prompt-text fan-out block + parent cross-partition-pass section, 1 PhaseConfig field + 1 phase_defaults merge, 1 REVIEWER-SYNC.md update, 1 Python-string fixture, 1 regression test file, 2 doc updates). Each change is mechanical and follows an existing pattern (REVIEWER_REFINE / REVIEWER_AGENT_DESIGN templates). No new subsystems, no schema migrations, no orchestrator routing changes, no MCP verb additions. The subagent fan-out is purely a prompt change leveraging the existing Task tool from the Claude Agent SDK. The single non-trivial design choice — whether to plumb diff metrics / contract through Python or self-gate in the prompt — has been resolved (Options 2B + 3B). The one load-bearing assumption that warrants an early smoke spike during implement-phase task-6 is decision-10 (Task subagents inherit MCP server access from the parent — see R-9). C5 specifies a probe + fallback (parent inlines the partition spec when subagents cannot reach MCP) so that if the spike fails, the implementation does not have to redesign — it falls back to a prompt-only contingency. This keeps complexity at 'medium' rather than 'high'.
